title: Roland Garros: overview

definition: Roland Garros in Paris, France: capacity about 15,000 (Chatrier), opened 1928.
description: Roland Garros stands in Paris, France: a 15,000 (Chatrier)-capacity venue opened in 1928, home to French Open. The cathedral of clay. Stadiums are the cathedrals of sport — concrete memory banks where generations experienced the same joys and heartbreaks. This database covers the ground's history, architecture, great events, and how to visit it.

title: History
d: Roland Garros opened in 1928. The cathedral of clay..
definition: Roland Garros opened in 1928. The cathedral of clay..
description: The history of Roland Garros begins in 1928. The cathedral of clay. Like all great grounds, it has been rebuilt, renamed, and reborn — stands rising where terraces stood, roofs arriving decades after the first kick. Its timeline is the timeline of its tenants' triumphs and the city's love affair with the game.

Great stadium design balances sightlines, acoustics, and atmosphere — the steepest stands feel closest, the roofs hold the roar in. Renovations keep adding hospitality while trying not to dilute the soul.

title: The tenants
d: Roland Garros is home to French Open.
definition: Roland Garros is home to French Open.
description: Roland Garros belongs to French Open — and to the fans who fill it. The tenant-club bond defines the ground's identity: the songs, the rituals, the expectation. When the team thrives the stadium shakes; when it struggles the old ground groans with it. You cannot separate the venue from its people.

title: Great matches
d: The greatest nights at Roland Garros live in legend.
definition: The greatest nights at Roland Garros live in legend.
description: The great nights at Roland Garros: title deciders, cup finals, impossible comebacks — the matches fans describe decades later as if they were yesterday. The cathedral of clay. Every old ground has a canon of such nights, and they are why the place matters: the stadium is the stage, but the drama is the point.

title: Finals hosted

definition: Roland Garros has hosted major finals and showpiece events.
description: Showpiece events at Roland Garros: cup finals, international tournaments, and one-off spectacles that put the ground on the world stage. Hosting a final is a civic honor — the city dresses up, the world watches, and the stadium joins the short list of venues that have seen it all.

title: Concerts and events
d: Roland Garros doubles as a concert and event venue.
definition: Roland Garros doubles as a concert and event venue.
description: Beyond sport, Roland Garros hosts concerts, ceremonies, and mega-events — the biggest stages need the biggest rooms. The ground's event history reads like pop culture itself. Multi-use keeps the economics working, though purists always prefer the roar of a matchday to anything else.

title: Visiting guide

definition: Visit Roland Garros: tours, matchdays, and practical tips.
description: Visiting Roland Garros: stadium tours run most days, taking in the dressing rooms, the tunnel, and the dugout — book ahead in season. On matchdays arrive early, learn the songs, and respect the home ends. Paris, France is best reached by public transport; driving on event days is for the patient.

title: Best seats

description: Seats at Roland Garros: behind the goal for the songs, halfway up the side for the tactical view, high corners for value. The famous ends have waiting lists measured in years; the family sections trade noise for comfort. Wherever you sit, the rule is the same — arrive early, stay late.

title: Attendance records
d: Roland Garros's biggest crowds and what drew them.
definition: Roland Garros's biggest crowds and what drew them.
description: The biggest crowds at Roland Garros came for the biggest occasions — derbies, finals, and farewell games. The cathedral of clay. Capacity has changed with all-seater conversions and expansions, so records from different eras are not directly comparable. What endures is the noise: full houses here are famously loud.

title: Fan culture

title: The future

definition: What is next for Roland Garros.
